key_insight: Pretrain perception with tri-modal (image + language + 3D motion/flow) signals so visual encoders learn dynamics-aware representations upstream, enabling robot policies to better understand and act on motion-relevant aspects of scenes.
problem_solved: Standard pretraining focuses on static recognition or vision-language alignment and leaves motion understanding to downstream policies, causing brittle or motion-agnostic perception for manipulation.
method: Construct image–language–3D-flow triplets from heterogeneous human and robot data to expose diverse motion cues during pretraining.
Train a multimodal encoder to align and fuse visual, textual, and 3D-motion features using dynamics-aware objectives so motion information is encoded in perception.
Transfer the learned representation to downstream robot manipulation tasks to improve motion-sensitive perception and policy performance.
impact: By pushing motion understanding into the perception backbone, DynaFLIP produces representations that are more useful, robust, and sample-efficient for robotic manipulation and other temporally-sensitive tasks.
visual_elements: Tri-modal schematic: image, text caption, and 3D-flow vectors combined into a single training triplet diagram.
Architecture block: encoder backbone with multimodal alignment and dynamics-aware objective blocks.
Before/after comparison: qualitative overlays showing improved 3D-flow-informed attention or feature maps on manipulation scenes.
Bar chart: relative gains in downstream manipulation benchmarks (e.g., accuracy, sample efficiency) when using DynaFLIP vs. static pretraining.
paper_title: DynaFLIP: Rethinking Robotics Perception via Tri-Modal-Dynamics Guided Representation
paper_authors: Jusuk Lee, Seungjae Lee, Jonghun Shin, Hoseong Jung, Sungha Kim
